Method of Attack: Encrypts victim's data using AES-128 encryption
Generates random 5 character extension appended to encrypted files
Uses unique 8 character victim ID derived from C:\ drive serial number and MAC address
Has working TOR command & control server
Sends base64 encoded AES-128 private decryption key and system info to C2 server
Displays ransom note with TOR payment site link and decryptor download
Decryptor connects to C2 server to check ransom payment status
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with files having targeted extensions such as .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .pdf, .jpg, .png, .sqlite, .php, .pptx, .mdb, .accdb, .txt, .csv, .sql, .html, .asp, .aspx, .dbf, .dbx, .dwg, .eps, .ibank, .indd, .jfif, .kdc, .mdb, .mdf, .odt, .orf, .p12, .p7b, .p7c, .pem, .pfx, .pps, .pst, .pub, .qbb, .qbw, .raw, .rtf, .sln, .svg, .tif, .tiff, .vcf, .wallet, .wpd and others
Indicators of Compromise: File extension appended to encrypted files (random 5 character extension, e.g., .a5zfn)
